title: Production of Metal Nanoparticles by Pulsed Laser-ablation in Liquids: A Tool for Studying the Antibacterial Properties of Nanoparticles
protocol: Assemble the ablation apparatus by placing a magnetic stir bar and a porous ablation stage inside a 50 mL glass beaker.
Place the beaker on a magnetic stir plate.
Set the Nd:YAG laser to operate at the fundamental wavelength of 1,064 nm with a pulse duration of 5 ns and a pulse repetition rate of 10 Hz.
Measure the energy per pulse using a laser power and energy meter; the required energy is 240-250 mJ.
Focus the beam beneath the target on the ablation stage using a 250 mm focal length converging lens (NA = 0.05).
Determine the spot size by placing a metal target on the stage and ablating with several laser pulses.
View the ablated target together with a micrometer slide on a CCD camera-equipped light microscope (4X objective) to measure the spot size.
Weigh a flat silver target using a microbalance to obtain the pre-ablation mass.
Adhere the silver target to the porous stage using double-sided carbon tape.
Add 40 mL of ablation liquid to the beaker.
The liquid height above the target is 11 mm.

Under constant stirring, move the computer-controlled motorized xy-stage in an elliptical pattern (dimensions: major axis = 2.09 cm, minor axis = 0.956 cm, area = 1.57 cm²) at a speed of 0.42 cm/s and ablate the target for 20-40 min.
Decant the nanoparticle solution from the beaker.
Measure the UV-visible light spectra (200-1,100 nm) to confirm the presence of nanoparticles.
Dilute highly concentrated NP solutions prior to measuring the UV-VIS spectrum if necessary.
Measure the hydrodynamic diameter of the NPs by dynamic light scattering (DLS) using a number distribution analysis method.
Dilute the NP solution 1:40 in the ablation solution and pipette 1 mL into a 1 cm plastic cuvette.
Utilize a measurement angle of 180° to measure the light scattering at a wavelength of 633 nm.
Dilute the NP solution 1:40 in double-distilled water.
Drop 2 μL of diluted NP solution onto a copper TEM grid pre-coated with lacey/thin carbon film.
Dry the NP solution overnight at room temperature under vacuum in a desiccator.
Dislodge any loosely attached NPs from the ablated metal target by sonicating it in distilled water for 1 min.
Dry the target under a stream of compressed air for 1 min.
Measure the mass of the target on a microbalance before and after ablation to quantify NP mass.
Dilute the NPs to a maximum concentration of 100 μg/mL in the same ablation solution used previously.
Transfer 15-17 mL of diluted NPs to a quartz cuvette containing a stir bar.
Place the cuvette on a magnetic stir-plate aligned parallel with the incoming laser.
Use a Nd:YAG laser system to produce 25 ps 532 nm laser pulses.
Focus the laser on the center of the solution using a 75 mm focal-length lens.
Irradiate the solution for 30 min to multiple hours, depending on the desired size.
Grow E. coli cultures (strain MG1655) overnight at 37 °C in Luria Broth (LB).
Dilute the overnight cultures to an optical density (λ = 600 nm) of 0.01 in fresh LB.
If NPs were synthesized in ablation media containing additives, add the respective chemical to the LB such that the concentration remains constant upon adding the NPs.
Prepare LB containing the appropriate concentration of additive (e.g., SDS) for maintaining consistency with ablation liquid concentrations.
Add NPs to diluted cultures at concentrations ranging from 0-50 µg/mL and grow cultures with shaking at 37 °C for an additional 2 h.
Treat E. coli with an antibiotic as a positive control for toxicity (e.g., 30 µg/mL kanamycin).
Serially dilute the culture samples 1:10 into fresh LB after incubation.
Spot 10 μL drops of each dilution onto LB agar plates, typically ranging from 10^4 to 10^8 fold dilutions.
Incubate the plates overnight at 37 °C and count colony forming units (cfu) the following morning.
